audit.whatIsWrong: Vault is labelled '(Dash/Blind)' in four fields (breakdown.trading, dosFull[2].d, report[3].t, report[5].t) and described as a knockback in whys[1], spikes[0].text and content.early ('she presses E herself, knocks you back'). Vault does not blind and does not knock you back.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'Quinn dashes to an enemy, dealing physical damage and slowing the target's Move Speed. Upon reaching the target, she leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away from the target.' She moves herself, not you. The interrupt is brief and it is an interrupt, not displacement. Whatever vision effect exists belongs to Blinding Assault (Q), a different slot entirely — the two got crossed. This changes the play: you are not being pushed out of your own root range, she is exiting it, so the answer is spacing and timing rather than bracing for a knockback.
audit.corrected: All seven occurrences restated as the leap-off-and-land-at-range interrupt, and the blind label moved off Vault.

audit.whatIsWrong: Behind Enemy Lines is a channel and the page never says so. Instead it repeatedly tells the reader they cannot stop her leaving: whys[4] 'she controls whether a fight happens, and she will always say no', content.mid 'do not waste R trying to hold her'.
audit.why: Quinn's R carries the channel flag — interruptible, any CC cancels it. Swain's Nevermove is hard CC on a 12s cooldown against a 3s-recast ultimate she uses to leave. That is the single most useful fact in this matchup and the page currently teaches the opposite: that she is unpunishable when she disengages. The mirror recorded the channel cancel from Quinn's side, so both directions should agree.
audit.corrected: tldr, dosFull[2].d, whys[4] and content.mid now state that a root cancels the channel.
sources: enemyKit R channel flag and text

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 3, 4 and 6 disagreed with the mirror in both layers.
audit.why: The mirror set rows 0, 3 and 4 to Quinn and row 6 to Swain, deliberately choosing Swain over the packet's 'Skill' at 2+ items. The prose here backs every one: content.early 'Quinn beats you cleanly from level 1 through 3', content.mid 'Levels 4 through 6 remain Quinn's lane', content.late 'At two items the matchup flips in your favor', plus whys[6] and spikes[3]. Rows 1, 2 and 5 already read Quinn.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 to Quinn and row 6 to Swain in both layers as one atomic group, ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns in the full layer at all, and content.mid tells the reader to 'mark 11 seconds in your head' after Vault.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s, so 11 seconds is the rank-2 number presented as the general case — a player counting 11 at rank 1 walks in one second early, which is exactly when it is back up. Blinding Assault is 1025 range on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s. Heightened Senses is 50/45/40/35/30s, a very long cooldown for something the page never mentions tracking.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into tldr, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, spikes[0].text; mid corrected to 12 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] credits Harrier with move speed. Harrier gives no movement speed.
audit.why: Harrier is Valor periodically marking a target so Quinn's first basic attack on it deals bonus physical damage. The attack speed and move speed come from Heightened Senses' passive, granted after she attacks a Harrier target. The mark and the steroid are two abilities and the page merged them.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] rewritten to credit Heightened Senses, keeping the Harrier mark as the trigger.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove's return-pass root is never stated, and dontsFull[2] is titled 'Get caught with E down' with a description about burning E on the wave.
audit.why: The root lands on the wave's RETURN trip, not the throw — against a champion whose whole defence is repositioning at 675 range, the timing of the return is the actual skill in the lane. The mirror calls this out explicitly as 'the actual dodging skill in this lane'.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[2].d now states the return pass.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 remain Quinn's lane — her poke accumulates faster than your fragment collection and her Vault keeps you locked out of any all-in that requires walking into her. Your job here is ruthless cooldown tracking: every time Quinn uses Vault, mark 11 seconds in your head and spend that window threatening W pressure or walking up to bait an E fish. At level 6 your Demonic Ascension heals through her auto-attack harassment in a prolonged fight, but she will simply disengage with Skystrike roams rather than stand in your drain; do not waste R trying to hold her — save it for a genuine all-in when Vault is confirmed down. Call your jungler for a dive once she has used Vault aggressively, because she has no second escape.
